stem: A healthy pregnant client with an uncomplicated pregnancy asks about exercise. Which recommendation is most appropriate?

options.A: Avoid starting aerobic exercise during pregnancy if you were previously sedentary; wait until after delivery to begin a regular program.
options.B: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week when there are no obstetric or medical contraindications; if new to exercise, start slowly and increase gradually.
options.C: Replace moderate-intensity activity with vigorous-intensity exercise during pregnancy even if you were not exercising vigorously before pregnancy.
options.D: Continue the same exercise plan throughout pregnancy without modification because normal physiologic changes do not require adjustment.

rationale: ACOG states that, in the absence of obstetric or medical complications or contraindications, physical activity during pregnancy is safe and desirable. Pregnant clients should ideally obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week. Clients who are new to exercise should start slowly and gradually increase activity, while some modification may be needed as pregnancy progresses. Therefore B is correct. A incorrectly delays safe activity until postpartum, C recommends vigorous exercise without regard to prior activity level, and D incorrectly excludes modification despite normal pregnancy-related changes.
educational_objective: Counsel a healthy client with an uncomplicated pregnancy to obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity weekly, with gradual progression and individualized adjustment when needed.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)

source_original.stem: A healthy pregnant client with an uncomplicated pregnancy asks about exercise. Which recommendation is most appropriate?

options.A: Limit activity to gentle stretching because moderate aerobic exercise is discouraged even when pregnancy is uncomplicated and no contraindication is present.
options.B: Aim for about 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week when there are no obstetric or medical contraindications, adjusting activity as needed.
options.C: Maintain the pre-pregnancy intensity target without adjusting for symptoms or obstetric changes because exercise recommendations remain fixed throughout pregnancy.
options.D: Begin vigorous conditioning even if previously sedentary because pregnancy is an appropriate time to increase exercise intensity rapidly for cardiovascular benefit.

source_original.rationale: For a healthy person with an uncomplicated pregnancy and no contraindications, regular physical activity is safe and desirable. Option B is correct because ACOG recommends about 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week, with adjustment as needed. Option A is unnecessarily restrictive. Option C ignores symptoms and obstetric changes. Option D inappropriately recommends rapid progression to vigorous conditioning for someone who may have been sedentary.
source_original.source_detail: ACOG — Exercise During Pregnancy: in uncomplicated pregnancy without medical/obstetric contraindications, physical activity is safe and desirable; pregnant individuals should generally obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week, with activity individualized and adjusted for symptoms/clinical changes. Current ACOG Exercise During Pregnancy patient/professional guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive care, immunization, pregnancy health promotion, adherence support and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the stem, construct and key B. Corrected the quantitative wording from 'about 150' to the source-supported 'at least 150 minutes'; rewrote distractors to test realistic errors about initiating exercise, vigorous intensity and failure to modify activity rather than relying on exaggerated statements.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current ACOG patient guidance plus ACOG Committee Opinion No. 804; NCSBN for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: ACOG pages remain live as current guidance and were rechecked 2026-08-16; no superseding ACOG exercise guideline identified
audit_findings.exact_locator: ACOG Exercise During Pregnancy > How much should I exercise?; Committee Opinion 804 > Recommendations/Recommending an Exercise Program
audit_findings.claim_audit: The 150-minute threshold, moderate intensity, uncomplicated-pregnancy condition, gradual progression for new exercisers and potential need for modification are directly supported by ACOG.

distractor_audit.A: ACOG permits initiation of safe physical activity during uncomplicated pregnancy and advises gradual progression for new exercisers.
distractor_audit.C: Vigorous activity continuation is tied to prior vigorous activity/fitness; it is not the default replacement for moderate activity in a previously non-vigorous exerciser.
distractor_audit.D: ACOG explicitly notes that modification may be necessary because of pregnancy-related changes.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B contains the recommended weekly target and appropriate progression without adding a conflicting exercise rule.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are exercise-program recommendations of similar scope; the key is not uniquely signaled by length or formatting.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance — antepartum health promotion and preventive education.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked threshold wording, contraindication scope, prior-activity logic, all distractors, rationale, objective, blueprint and second-answer risk from zero; B remained uniquely best.
